rules.statement: TL-UL host drivers in this library are not required to drive valid signals LOW for at least 100 cycles during reset, unlike TileLink 1.7.1.
TL-UL devices tolerate reset windows shorter than 100 cycles.
Request steering must be a function of the address only; a_source and a_user must not enter into the address calculation.
A host may use a_source/d_source to ascribe request identifiers, since TL-UL does not guarantee in-order responses.
The fabric architect must ensure AIW covers the host outstanding requests and the maximum source ID growth added by bus primitives.

rules.condition: converting from a host such as AXI using RID or WID
rules.statement: The fabric must provide enough host ID bits to maintain those ID values.

rules.condition: a primitive adds source ID bits
rules.statement: The primitive shifts a_source left and post-pends sub-source bits; on the response it shifts them off, shifting zeros into the top, and returns the result on d_source.
Assertions should ensure no significant bits of a_source are lost in M:1 sockets.
Hosts may only use the low bits of the source identifier and must not assume all AIW bits are returned intact.
Devices must return the associated a_source on the response d_source.
Bus hosts and devices must understand the usage of user bits and apply them appropriately.
User bits follow the same timing as source ID bits: a_user matches a_source and d_user matches d_source.
The bus fabric must not rely on user bits for transport and must pass them on blindly; usage must be assigned project-wide.
a_opcode may designate a write (Put) or read (Get); writes may be full (PutFullData) or partial (PutPartialData).
TL-UL hosts in this project should not use non-contiguous a_mask values such as 0b1001.

rules.condition: device does not support a subword mask
rules.statement: Devices may assert d_error if they do not support a particular subword a_mask.
For PutFullData, a_size should be 'h2 for a 32b write ('h3 for 64b bus).
For PutPartialData, a_size should encode 2^a_size bytes and the a_mask bits should indicate the valid byte lanes.
Devices should return an error for undefined request opcodes.
Undefined response opcodes d_opcode 3'b01x and 3'b1xx should return an error.
